card.name: Small linking words in old-style prose
card.fires_on: Small words such as to, this, of, a and far inside long, formal sentences of 19th-century style prose (history, essays, memoirs). The marked word sits mid-clause, before the main noun or verb.

modes.label: Infinitive 'to'
modes.description: The word 'to' in a formal clause, often after 'either' or 'or'.
modes.example: or<< to>> accelerate a return of peace.

modes.label: Determiners and 'of'
modes.description: Words like this, a or of that come before a noun in old historical prose.
modes.example: distinguished<< this>> part of the continent in later times.

modes.label: Descriptive word before noun
modes.description: A noun or adjective in a literary phrase, such as gun or glowing.
modes.example: never heard a hostile<< gun>> before

card.plain: It fires on small linking words in long, old-fashioned essay or history prose, not on medical wording.
